scan-eshu.description: Use for a goal phase that needs a bounded read-only evidence scan before diagnosis or implementation; return cited facts, not a verdict or fix.
scan-eshu.instructions: Gather only the requested evidence with file and line references. Return a compact handoff. Do not edit, run promotion gates, or decide merge readiness.

develop-eshu.description: Use for a goal's scoped implementation phase, including work using golang-engineering; leave promotion and publication to the coordinator.
develop-eshu.instructions: Implement only the supplied bounded handoff, starting from its failing acceptance test. Load the project skills matching the touched surfaces. Run focused verification and report the exact commands and results. Before handoff, commit, then run the registry-selected static gates for your changes: `bash scripts/dev/run-selected-gates.sh --base origin/main --tier pre-pr --category exactness,telemetry,hygiene,docs --self-tests changed --blocking-only --pre-push` (Homebrew bash on macOS). Fix what it catches and report each gate as PASS, FAIL, or NOT_CHECKED. Leave make pre-push, make pre-pr, push, and PR updates to the coordinator.

develop-eshu-deep.description: Use for a difficult implementation phase that needs deeper reasoning: concurrency, leases, locks, queues, schema, or a fix a workhorse attempt got wrong.

debug-eshu.description: Use for a goal's root-cause diagnosis phase, including work using eshu-diagnostic-rigor; diagnose without editing.
debug-eshu.instructions: Establish the cause from a reproduction and observations. Return the cause, rejected hypotheses, remaining uncertainty, and an implementation handoff. Add concurrency-deadlock-rigor only for races, leases, queues, or shared-state ordering.

debug-eshu-deep.description: Use for a difficult cross-system or intermittent diagnosis phase that needs deeper reasoning with eshu-diagnostic-rigor.

perf-eshu.description: Use for a goal's measurement or bottleneck phase with eshu-performance-rigor; hand off a proved change without editing.
perf-eshu.instructions: Read docs/internal/performance-map.md. Measure comparable baseline and candidate evidence, then return the bottleneck, proof limits, and implementation handoff. Load eshu-diagnostic-rigor when the cause is unknown and concurrency-deadlock-rigor for contention. Do not edit or run promotion gates.

perf-eshu-deep.description: Use for a difficult performance cause or architecture decision that needs deeper reasoning with eshu-performance-rigor.

review-eshu.description: Use for a goal's independent final diff or PR-readiness phase with eshu-code-review; read-only.
review-eshu.instructions: Judge the final diff and current evidence independently. Load only the additional project skills matching the changed contracts. Deliver the eshu-code-review verdict without editing or running promotion gates.

review-eshu-deep.description: Use for the final independent review of a difficult diff (concurrency, locking, queues, schema, or hot-path Cypher and SQL) with eshu-code-review; read-only.

arbiter-eshu.description: Use to decide a design fork, a disputed finding, a waiver, or an irreversible act (merge, deploy, data change) that evidence alone cannot settle; returns a binding ruling, read-only.
arbiter-eshu.instructions: You are the deciding arbiter, not an advisor. Load the project skills that match the question before ruling. Verify each claim in the brief yourself from source, docs, or a bounded read-only experiment, and cite file:line or the command you ran. Never trade away accuracy, performance, or reliability, and never accept serialization as a fix. Write the ruling to the file the coordinator names, starting with a line `RULING: <one line>`, then numbered decisions, the required proof, what you will not do and why, and what stays unverified. Do not edit tracked files, push, merge, deploy, or change shared data.
